pages.title: A08 · Joins and unions
lede: Objective (S3): combine DataFrames with inner, left, broadcast, multi-key and cross joins, union and union all.
Retail data: customers 4, orders 4 (5004 has no customer), products 3, order_items 5. Order 5004 is the orphan.

blocks.heading: 1. Inner vs left vs left anti
blocks.code:
orders.join(customers, "customer_id").count()               # 3  inner is the default, drops 5004 silently
orders.join(customers, "customer_id", "left").count()       # 4  keeps every order, NULL name and state for 5004
orders.join(customers, "customer_id", "left_anti").count()  # 1  orphans: left rows with no match
blocks.note: String or list key keeps one key column. An expression (a.id == b.id) keeps both, so select is ambiguous.

blocks.heading: 2. Multiple keys and duplicate dimension keys
blocks.code:
order_items.join(returns, "order_id").count()                # 2  wrong: both lines of 5001 match
order_items.join(returns, ["order_id", "line_no"]).count()   # 1  full key
orders.join(dup_customers, "customer_id", "left").count()    # 6  customer 101 twice: rows multiply
blocks.note: Join on the full key. Check the dimension key is unique before you join.

blocks.heading: 3. Broadcast joins
blocks.note: Broadcast the small right side. Auto broadcast under 10 MB (Spark default). Adaptive Query Execution (AQE) can switch at run time. A hint is a suggestion.

blocks.heading: 4. Cross join
blocks.note: Use only when you want every combination. Check both counts first.

pages.title: Unions, silver build, checklist, snippet

blocks.heading: 5. union vs union all vs unionByName
blocks.code:
SQL UNION: dups removed. SQL UNION ALL: dups kept. Both match columns by position.
df.union(df2) = df.unionAll(df2): dups kept, by position.   df.unionByName(df2): by name.
orders_mon.union(orders_resend).count()     # 4   (.distinct().count() -> 3)
orders_mon.union(store)                     # customer 103 lands in order_id, no error
orders_mon.unionByName(extra, allowMissingColumns=True)   # both fail NUM_COLUMNS_MISMATCH without it
blocks.note: Memory trick: PySpark union is UNION ALL in disguise. It keeps every row and matches columns by position.

blocks.heading: 6. On the job: silver_order_lines
blocks.code:
order_lines = (order_items.join(orders, "order_id")                 # fact to fact: shuffle
  .join(broadcast(customers), "customer_id", "left")                 # small dim: broadcast, keep orphans
  .join(broadcast(products), "product_id")
  .withColumn("line_total", F.col("quantity") * F.col("price")))     # 5 rows, total 84.00
blocks.note: An inner customer join gives 4 lines and 72.00: order 5004 (12.00) vanishes with no error.

blocks.heading: 7. Join-choice checklist
blocks.text: 1) Keys: full key, unique dimension key, same types. 2) Type: every fact row = left, only matches = inner, every combination = crossJoin after counting. 3) Broadcast the small right side, never the fact table. 4) union keeps dups, matches by position: unionByName for other sources. 5) Reconcile rows in, out, unmatched.

blocks.heading: 8. Reusable snippet: join_orders_to_customers
Practice challenge
blocks.text: Q1 orders right join customers: 5. Q2 crossJoin, filter TX: 6. Q3 orders_resend.join(orders_mon, "order_id", "left_anti"): 1 row (5003). Exam-style (2 billion order_items, 5,000 products, keep every line): order_items.join(broadcast(products), "product_id", "left").
